atDirectives.name: @tailwind
atDirectives.description: Use the `@tailwind` directive to insert Tailwind's `base`, `components`, `utilities` and `screens` styles into your CSS.

atDirectives.name: @apply
atDirectives.description: Use the `@apply` directive to inline any existing utility classes into your own custom CSS. This is useful when you find a common utility pattern in your HTML that you’d like to extract to a new component.

atDirectives.name: @responsive
@screen
@variants
@container
atDirectives.description: Container queries enable you to apply styles to an element based on the size of the element's container. If, for example, a container has less space available in the surrounding context, you can hide certain elements or use smaller fonts. Container queries are an alternative to media queries, which apply styles to elements based on viewport size or other device characteristics

atDirectives.name: @theme
@utility
atDirectives.description: Use the `@utility` directive to register low-level utility classes in Tailwind’s layer system. This allows fine-grained control over where and how your custom utilities are injected into the final CSS.
